final_message:
DONE

I've built the Excel tracker and a short Word memo answering the three questions. I recalculated all 1,410 formulas in the workbook and each matches its stored value. I also re-read the exception notes and the action table against the rules I stated, and fixed a few wording mismatches.

**Answers**
1. **Departments:** none are at risk. All five are within 95%–105%: Research 101.6%, IT 101.5%, PMO 101.1%, Professional Education 98.3%, Communications 96.5%. The company overall is at 100.0%.
2. **Individuals:** five people are flagged. Four part-timers are above 90% and at burnout risk: Trevor Shaw 103.8%, Zach Foster 95.0%, Isaac Turner 91.2% and Will Smith 91.2%. Priya Desai is below 60% at 53.8%. Her low rate comes almost entirely from the week of 24 March, when she recorded only 10 admin hours; the first three weeks alone give 71.7%. Her timesheet should be checked before acting on this.
3. **Projects:** six of nine went over budget. Website Redesign (+79 hrs, 139.5%) and IT Implementation (+57 hrs, 115.2%) are the big overruns. The others are Customer Onboarding Platform +26, Annual Plan +14, Planned Giving Campaign +4 and Adult Outpatient Pavilion Construction +1. In total, 2,488 hours were charged against 2,350 budgeted.

**How I measured individuals:** the rate is project hours (logged admin hours removed) divided by full monthly capacity. A fully loaded person therefore shows about 85%, which sits between the 60% and 90% thresholds. I also tried the other reading, dividing by 85% of capacity. Under that version 18 of 23 people would be above 90% and nobody below 60%, so the thresholds would flag almost everyone. The workbook states which method I used and why.

**Data issues, all logged in the workbook:**
- **Ellen Zhu** logged 155 hours in the timekeeping export but is not one of the 23 people in the registry. I left her out of the individual and department figures because her role and capacity are unknown. Her hours do count toward the project totals because they were charged to projects. Without them, Customer Onboarding would be within budget; HR should confirm who she is.
- **31 March is missing** from the export, which covers 3–28 March. I set monthly capacity to four weeks (160 hours full-time, 80 part-time) to match. Any 31 March hours would only add to the project overruns.
- **Admin time:** every full-time employee logged more admin than the 15% allowance, George Lin the most at 29.4%. This lowers their project rates.
- The `workspace/` and `attachments/` folders mentioned in the brief don't exist, so I used only the three reference files.

The workbook's Summary tab includes a table of recommended actions with owners and timing.

Files are in `outputs/`:
- `Workload_Distribution_Tracker_March2025.xlsx`
- `Workload_Distribution_Brief_Responses_March2025.docx`
